Moderately positive with a cautious policy tilt. The FOMC highlights strong job gains and low unemployment, consistent with New Keynesian models where tighter labor markets raise real marginal costs and near‑term inflation pressures (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005). The commitment to a symmetric 2% objective and the note that market-based inflation compensation has risen but remains low point to anchored expectations, aligning with inflation-targeting frameworks that emphasize expectations management (Svensson and Woodford, 2005) and reduce average inflation bias. Gradualism and a funds rate “below longer-run” levels fit rule-like policy smoothing (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor-style rules), while acknowledging the cost channel can make rate hikes temporarily cost‑push (Ravenna and Walsh, 2006). Still, moderation in household spending/business investment and continued balance-sheet runoff temper the tone. Overall assessment: mildly positive for the growth outlook, tempered by ongoing normalization.
